DroidDeck · AYANEO Pocket FIT · Adreno 750 · 144 Hz

DD 0.6.0 Stable and now

DroidDeck's performance fixes stop DroidDeck, gamescope and Wine from waiting on each other every frame, and with PR #1697 Windows games get the fastest core as CPU 0. Since PRs #1706–#1708 gamescope and the compositor handle each new frame as soon as it arrives, and Steam's start no longer slows the first seconds of a game. The first fixes started as the Performance mode switch; since PR #1650 every session runs that way, and Steam's Frame Limit in the Quick Access menu is the only frame limit.

AIO Graphics Test 2.2.0, average fps, no frame limit, Turnip, same Pocket FIT; bars scaled per API; the percentage is DroidDeck now as a share of the Winlator fork. DD 0.6.0 Stable: the 2026-10-22 release had none of these fixes; measured 2026-10-26 with every fix switched off (the old Performance mode switch off), 15 s runs, the middle of three: frame rates swung widely then (the range is under each screenshot below). DroidDeck latest: 2026-10-28, DroidDeck main 213c2da5 (every fix on, including PRs #1706–#1708); DirectDraw / D3D7 on the PR #1715 build 8c94cb85, merged as main 9d82df69 (the review changes after it do not touch the default path), DroidDeck-Proton 11-11.9, on battery, 30 s runs, best of two. Winlator fork: 2026-10-21, 15 s runs, best of two. DirectDraw / Direct3D 7 run through WineD3D on OpenGL; since PR #1715 OpenGL no longer waits for each screen refresh while Steam's Frame Limit is off (AIO D3D7 144 → 2,345 fps), and the Frame Limit still holds it when on (72 → 71.9 fps). Direct3D 8 runs through WineD3D by default; the per-game PROTON_DXVK_D3D8 option raises AIO D3D8 2,408 → 3,097 (measured 2026-10-25).

Screenshots taken on the same Pocket FIT. DiRT and GTA IV on 2026-10-27, same in-game settings. DroidDeck: DroidDeck-Proton 11-11.9; the DiRT run is from before the fastest-core fix, which doesn't change DiRT. Winlator fork: its Proton 11 ARM64EC container. The overlay in the corner tells them apart: green is DroidDeck's, pink is the Winlator fork's. Dead Cells on 2026-10-28, one moment each, not an average. DroidDeck: the PR #1715 build 8c94cb85 (the code now in main 9d82df69), DroidDeck-Proton 11-11.9. There the game's own frame rate is in Steam's bar across the top; DroidDeck's green box counts the frames sent to the 144 Hz screen. Another Crab's Treasure on 2026-10-29, one moment each, not an average, same in-game settings (1280 × 720, High, textures Highest, V-Sync off, no FPS limit), frame generation off in both. Its numbers are read off each app's HUD: frame rate, frame time, GPU and CPU load, battery power draw. DroidDeck: the PR #1763 build a13c038c, DroidDeck-Proton 11-11.9. There DroidDeck's overlay is the new blue HUD at the top; the white panel on the left or along the top is the Pocket FIT's own overlay.

Whole-device power from the battery (unplugged, screen brightness fixed, fan on high), averaged over each run's benchmark window; busy cores = CPU use across all 8 cores; AIO Direct3D 11 cube, 45 s runs, Turnip, measured 2026-10-26 on the Performance mode test build. With no limit the fixes draw 3.6× the frames for 42 % more power. The 60 fps rows used the app's own frame limiter, which DroidDeck has since replaced with Steam's Frame Limit (PR #1616, PR #1650); they have not been re-measured with Steam's limit.

Numbers come from AIO's results files, the games' own benchmark results and the battery's own current and voltage readings, not from the screenshots. In DroidDeck: the compositor and swapchain changes (PR #1563, always on since PR #1650), gamescope 3.16.29-p13 → p17 (PR #1672) → p18 (PR #1706, with upstream fence fixes by Matthew Schwartz), the Wine fix in DroidDeck-Proton 11-11.6 and later, the screen tick thread (PR #1678), fastest-first cores (PR #1697, merged), new frames drawn on arrival (PR #1707), Steam's start-up driver check skipped (PR #1708) and OpenGL games no longer wait for each screen refresh (PR #1715).
